solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Old Nazi full of resentment for one who's succeeded

indicators.note: the Nazi's name is filled with the word for resentment, so it goes around it

parts.note: Rudolf Hess was Hitler's deputy
resentment is ire, anger

explanation.surface: A grim picture of an elderly Nazi still seething with grievance against a successful person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one who's succeeded' reads as someone who has done well, but here it means one who has come into an inheritance.
explanation.definitionFit: A female inheritor is one who succeeds to an estate or title on a death.

clue.text: Heroic adventure about the same eruption

indicators.note: the heroic tale goes around the Latin word

parts.note: an epic is a heroic tale of adventure
idem is Latin for the same

explanation.surface: A heroic adventure story about a volcanic eruption.
explanation.definitionFit: An epidemic is a sudden outbreak of disease, a figurative eruption.

clue.text: One getting peaches regularly in flower

indicators.note: the picked letters go inside the flowing word

parts.note: a river is a flower, something that flows

indicators.note: every other letter of peaches is taken

explanation.surface: Someone regularly given peaches while the trees are in blossom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a crossword trick: a thing that flows, a river, not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A receiver is a person who receives or gets something, a recipient.

clue.text: It could get you to plastered drywall's top when rebuilding

definitions.text: It could get you to plastered drywall's top when rebuilding

indicators.note: rebuilding means the letters are reassembled in a new order
only the first letter of drywall is used

explanation.surface: A builder reaching the top of a newly plastered wall during a renovation.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram is PLASTERED plus D; the whole clue also describes a builder's means of reaching the top of a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Folding steps are what a decorator climbs to reach the upper part of a wall.

clue.text: Region in central Zanzibar, as some might see it

indicators.note: the letter I looks like a Roman numeral, so some read it as a number
the middle two letters of Zanzibar are taken

explanation.surface: An area in the middle of Zanzibar, according to some people's view.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of ZANZIBAR is ZI; reading I as the Roman numeral for 1 gives Z ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A zone is an area or region distinguished from its surroundings.

clue.text: Business having turned sour since sacking Poles

parts.note: milk that has turned sour is off

indicators.note: sacking means removing, so the pole letters are dismissed

parts.note: taken as written
S and N are the south and north poles

explanation.surface: A business gone sour since it sacked its Polish workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like Polish people; here it is the abbreviations for north and south.
explanation.definitionFit: An office is a place of business, or a post or function, the business someone has.

clue.text: Fitting doctrine following initiation of blood rite

indicators.note: the fitting and doctrine words come after the opening letter
the initiation, or beginning, of blood is its first letter

parts.note: apt means fitting, suitable
an ism is a doctrine or belief

explanation.surface: A doctrine about the proper way to carry out a blood ritual of initiation.
explanation.definitionFit: Baptism is the Christian sacrament of initiation, a ritual or ceremony.

clue.text: Noble, unrivalled Liberal must stand down

indicators.note: standing down means leaving, so the abbreviation is removed

parts.note: peerless means without equal

explanation.surface: A political tale: an unrivalled Liberal politician forced to resign.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman holding a title in the peerage, such as a countess, is a noble.

clue.text: 3-D object with internal 2-D fuse

indicators.note: the two-dimensional word sits inside the solid shape's name

parts.note: a cone is a solid, three-dimensional shape
a flat thing has only two dimensions

explanation.surface: Reads like geometry or a 3-D printing instruction: a solid with a flat insert forming a fuse.
explanation.definitionFit: To fuse two things is to merge or combine them into one, a synonym.

clue.text: Room in church with half-hearted cat put outside

indicators.note: the trimmed cat word is placed around the church abbreviation
the doubled letter at the word's heart loses one of its pair

parts.note: a kitten is a young cat

explanation.surface: A churchgoer reluctantly turning the cat out of the building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' removes one of the two central Ts, leaving KITEN, which 'put outside' wraps around CH.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen is the room of a house where food is cooked, an example of a room.

clue.text: Leading lady in lingerie holding first show

indicators.note: the designer's surname contains the abbreviation

parts.note: Janet Reger was a leading British designer of luxury lingerie
1st, written IST, is the abbreviation of first

explanation.surface: Suggests a star actress in underwear at a premiere.
explanation.walkthrough: Janet Reger was a famous British lingerie designer, so 'leading lady in lingerie' is her name, not an actress.
explanation.definitionFit: To register an emotion is to show or display it on one's face, a verb synonym.

clue.text: De Niro has played an old countryman

indicators.note: played suggests the letters are acted out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Robert De Niro once took the role of an elderly rural man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old countryman' looks like a rustic; it is a citizen of a former country, Rhodesia (now Zimbabwe).
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of the former state of Rhodesia, now Zimbabwe, is a compatriot of a vanished nation.

clue.text: Servant, at first meek, affable but no good

indicators.note: only the opening letter of meek is used
the abbreviation for good is dropped from the friendly word

parts.note: affable means genial, friendly

explanation.surface: Describes a servant who begins meek and pleasant but turns out to be useless.
explanation.definitionFit: A menial, used as a noun, is a domestic servant or drudge doing lowly work.

clue.text: Ideal secretary backed over essay about nothing

indicators.note: backed means the letters run in reverse

parts.note: PA, personal assistant, is a secretary
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over

indicators.note: the essay goes around the zero

parts.note: a thesis is a long essay
O, zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: An office scene: a secretary returns an essay about nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is not a positional word here but the cricket abbreviation O, a standalone piece between the reversed secretary and the essay.
explanation.definitionFit: An apotheosis is the perfect example or highest embodiment of something, i.e. the ideal.

clue.text: Timely new bouquet delivered as support for fling

indicators.note: in a down entry the later pieces are placed beneath, supporting the first

parts.note: to heave is to fling or throw

indicators.note: delivered means spoken, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: a bouquet is a scent, as of wine

explanation.surface: A romantic gesture: a fresh bouquet arriving just in time to keep an affair going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivered' looks like flowers being brought, but it signals speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Something providential, arriving at just the right moment, is opportune.

clue.text: Extra roomy

definitions.meaning: in cricket a ... is an extra, a run given for a ball bowled out of the batter's reach

explanation.surface: Extra roomy: a phrase from clothing or car advertising.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, extras are runs not scored off the bat; a ball bowled too far from the batter is one kind.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the cricket extra; the other is the adjective for broad or spacious.

clue.text: Dog is free, say, to run round tail

parts.note: to rid is to free or clear

indicators.note: running round sends the letters in the opposite direction

parts.note: eg, for example, is signalled by say
the tail is the back or rear end

explanation.surface: A dog let loose, going round chasing its own tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhodesian ridgeback is a breed of hound with a ridge of hair along its spine.

clue.text: Mark turned up with new author that's penned 'Gordon woz 'ere'

indicators.note: the rearranged author is enclosed by the mark letters
in a down entry, turned up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: MK is the abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

indicators.note: new means the letters are made fresh in another order

explanation.surface: A writer's graffiti scrawled by Gordon, like a tourist's mark.
explanation.walkthrough: General Gordon was killed at the siege of this city in 1885, so it is where Gordon was.
explanation.definitionFit: General Charles Gordon defended the Sudanese capital and died there, so graffiti claiming his presence fits.

clue.text: Union leader removed in time-wasting

indicators.note: the first letter is taken off the front

parts.note: dalliance is idle time-wasting

explanation.surface: A trade union's leader sacked for wasting time.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance is a union or partnership formed for mutual benefit.

clue.text: Exhausted by delay over town and county

parts.note: done means exhausted, worn out

indicators.note: over means turned the other way

parts.note: a lag is a delay

explanation.surface: Someone worn out by a hold-up involving town and county matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Donegal is both a town and a county in the north-west of Ireland.

clue.text: Sweeping practice — store staff may each pursue it

definitions.text: practice — store staff may each pursue it
definitions.meaning: practice, store and staff can each follow the word to make a familiar phrase

explanation.surface: A cleaning routine that every shop worker might follow.
explanation.walkthrough: Each of practice, store and staff completes a common phrase after the answer, such as the practice of a family doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweeping changes are broad and all-embracing, not specific.

clue.text: Divine note taken from sermon

indicators.note: the musical note is removed from the sermon

parts.note: a homily is a sermon
mi is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A churchgoer jotting down a note from a sermon on divine matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Holy and divine are synonyms meaning sacred, of God.

clue.text: Gush from modified e-vaporiser

indicators.note: modified means the letters are changed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An outpouring of steam from a tinkered-with e-cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gush' looks like the vapour pouring out, but it is the verb for effusive praise.
explanation.definitionFit: To gush is to speak with excessive enthusiasm, i.e. to flatter too much.

clue.text: Choice to lower head when getting draught

indicators.note: the opening letter is moved down to a lower place in the word

parts.note: an option is a choice

explanation.surface: Choosing to bow one's head while taking a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A potion is a drink of medicine or magic, a draught.

clue.text: King, I see, managed to circulate port

indicators.note: circulating sends the whole string round the other way

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
v, from Latin vide, means see
ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: A king noticing that someone arranged for something to be passed around.
explanation.definitionFit: Narvik is a Norwegian seaport, an example of a port.

clue.text: Choosing building that's changed hands

indicators.note: R for right is swapped for L for left, a change of hand

parts.note: an erection is a building

explanation.surface: A property that has been sold on to a new owner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed hands' looks like a sale, but it swaps R (right) for L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: An election is the act of choosing, especially by voting.

clue.text: Duty paid by the Telegraph?

parts.note: on means paid by, as in drinks are on me
the newspaper speaking of itself says us

explanation.surface: Asks whether a tax is paid by the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a responsibility or obligation, a duty.

clue.text: Perhaps Tess now embraces love-in

indicators.note: the word for now holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: here can mean now, at this point
love is O, the zero score in tennis, followed by IN

explanation.surface: Suggests Tess joining a hippy love-in.
explanation.definitionFit: Tess is the central female character of Hardy's Tess of the d'Urbervilles, an example of a leading lady.

clue.text: Never opened trite magazine, or something similar

indicators.note: neither word is allowed its opening letter, so both first letters go

parts.note: banal means trite, hackneyed
Vogue is a fashion magazine

explanation.surface: Someone who never opened a trite magazine, or anything like it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Never opened' removes the first letter of both words: B from BANAL and V from VOGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: An analogue is a thing comparable or corresponding to another, a parallel.

clue.text: You'd walk if this ran a cover-up for corporation

indicators.note: the word for ran wraps around the belly word

parts.note: sped means ran quickly
corporation is an old jokey word for a pot belly, or tum

explanation.surface: Reads like a scandal: a running cover-up on behalf of a company.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batter who is out leaves the field, called walking; being caught out of the crease by the wicketkeeper is one way out.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket batter dismissed by the wicketkeeper breaking the wicket must leave the field.
